audit.whatIsWrong: content win[4] reads Skill at Level 6 while whys[4] says 'Level 6 is still yours — your Q pattern and drain beat him before his Hemoplague spike matters'. The packet chart gives Aatrox six stages and Vladimir only Two+ items.
audit.why: Hemoplague is a 120s delayed area amp; it does nothing for Vladimir's solo durability at level 6, which is why the entry's own reasoning keeps that stage with Aatrox. 50.56% over 2870 games.
audit.corrected: Level 6 reads Aatrox; Two+ items stays Vladimir.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sanguine Pool is the pivot of every spike and the entry never gives its cooldown, which is the whole reason the early game is winnable.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16 — twenty-eight seconds at rank 1, against a 6s Darkin Blade and a 9s Umbral Dash. That is not a tool he can hold for every trade; it is the single longest basic-ability cooldown you will face in lane. Transfusion is 9s falling to 4.6s and Hemoplague a flat 120s.
audit.corrected: 28s Sanguine Pool, 9s Transfusion and 120s Hemoplague written into spikes[1], mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry writes 'Sanguine Pool (E)' in spikes[1] and wants.you[2]. Sanguine Pool is his W. His E is Tides of Blood. It also describes Pool as a way for him to 'body your combo', which understates it: he is untargetable for two full seconds, so anything you commit mid-Pool is thrown away entirely rather than reduced.
audit.why: Riot's text: Sanguine Pool — 'Vladimir sinks into a pool of blood, becoming untargetable for 2 seconds. Additionally, enemies on the pool are slowed and Vladimir siphons life from them.' Untargetable is the key word: Deathbringer Stance, the third-Q knockup and Infernal Chains all fizzle, and he heals off you while you stand in it. The correct play is to hold the knockup, walk off the pool, and re-commit — not to burst faster.
audit.corrected: Pool corrected to the W slot, its 2s untargetability stated, and the instruction changed from 'bait Pool' to 'hold your commit and step off the pool while it runs'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood is never named anywhere in the entry, and it is the ability he actually pokes with.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Vladimir pays his own health to charge up a reservoir of blood which, when released, deals damage in the area around him but can be blocked by enemy units.' Two things follow that the entry never tells the player: his poke costs him health, so a Vlad who has been charging E is already chipping himself, and the damage is blocked by units — standing with minions between you and him removes it.
audit.corrected: Tides of Blood named in early with the minion-block and self-damage facts.

edits.before: Even at 6 you hold the edge, but respect Hemoplague (R) and Sanguine Pool (E) — bait Pool before you commit your Q sweetspot so his combo-dodge can't waste your all-in.
edits.after: Even at 6 you hold the edge, but Sanguine Pool (W, 28s) makes him untargetable for 2 seconds — hold the third-Q knockup, walk off the pool, then re-commit into that 28s gap.

edits.before: Level 1-2 favours Aatrox: Vlad's Transfusion (Q) heals every last-hit but he's a low-mobility, low-damage early laner, so your base stats and durability let you push in and pressure him before his kit spikes. Bring Grievous Wounds to blunt his heals. Don't over-invest E charges — just farm, trade when your passive is up, and set up for your level-3 spike.
edits.after: Level 1-2 favours Aatrox: Transfusion (9s) heals him off every last-hit, but he is low-mobility and low-damage early, so your stats let you pressure him first. Tides of Blood costs him his own health and is blocked by units, so stand with minions between you and take it off the table. Buy Grievous Wounds, farm, and set up your level-3 spike.

edits.before: Levels 3 through your first item all favour Aatrox — your Q pattern and drain are online before Vlad's kit comes together, so all-in him, land the knockup, and stack Grievous Wounds pressure. His one out is Sanguine Pool, which lets him body your combo, so bait Pool first and trade when it's on cooldown. Kill him repeatedly in this pre-item window, because every item he buys pulls him toward his unkillable late game.
edits.after: Levels 3 through your first item all favour Aatrox — your Q pattern is online before his kit is, so all-in, land the knockup, and keep Grievous Wounds on him. His one out is Sanguine Pool (W): two seconds untargetable, in which every ability you throw is wasted and he siphons off you. Hold your combo, step off the pool, and re-commit — at 28s rank 1 it will not be back. Kill him repeatedly now.

edits.before: Vladimir out-scales almost every bruiser. With items his Transfusion healing, Pool immunity window, and Hemoplague damage amp make him extremely hard to kill in a drawn-out fight, and he out-teamfights you. Grievous Wounds is mandatory all game. Try to end the lane before he ramps, and in the late game play around his Pool cooldown rather than expecting to solo him.
edits.after: Vladimir out-scales almost every bruiser. With items Transfusion drops to 4.6s, Sanguine Pool to 16s, and a 120s Hemoplague amps everything that lands on your team while healing him per champion hit. Grievous Wounds is mandatory all game. End the lane before he ramps, and late play around the Pool timer rather than expecting to solo him.

edits.before: Bait Sanguine Pool (E) before committing your Q sweetspot
edits.after: Hold your knockup through his 2s Sanguine Pool (W) window

edits.before: Vladimir changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Vladimir pool, empowered Q, R, and scaling. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Vladimir wants to keep distance, poke Aatrox before he can reach the wave, and punish missed Qs with ranged damage or crowd control.
edits.after: Vladimir changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Sanguine Pool (W, 28s), two seconds of untargetability that void anything committed into them while he siphons himself back up off the slow beneath him. Aatrox wins by holding the third Darkin Blade swing until the pool ends, standing behind minions so Tides of Blood is blocked, and keeping Grievous Wounds on him from the first back.

edits.before: Vladimir pool, empowered Q, R, and scaling

notes: The wrong-slot error ('Sanguine Pool (E)') appears twice in this matchup alone and Tides of Blood is never named anywhere in the Aatrox file for Vladimir. Both are likely to recur across the other Vladimir matchups in champ-data/content — worth a file-wide grep for 'Sanguine Pool (E)'.
